title: Best Dehumidifier for Wet Carpet (2026): Flooded Carpet Picks
h1: The Best Dehumidifiers for Wet Carpet
dek: A soaked carpet has about two days before it starts to smell. The right machine, and the right order of steps, decides whether you save it.
description: The best dehumidifier for wet carpet, from LGR units for flooded rooms to a household pump model for spills, plus when to pull the pad and how long it takes.
intro: The best **dehumidifier for wet carpet** is the one that keeps pulling water out of the air after the obvious puddles are gone, because that's when carpet, pad and subfloor are still giving up moisture. This page is for anyone staring at a soaked rug after a washer overflow, a burst supply line or a flooded basement. Three things matter most: low-grain drying power that holds up as the room gets drier, a pump so the machine runs all night without a full bucket, and enough airflow across the carpet to make the water evaporate in the first place. Our top pick, the **AlorAir Storm LGR Extreme**, covers all three for a carpeted room or a typical basement.

For one wet bedroom, the lighter **Dri-Eaz LGR 5000Li** is easier to carry upstairs; for a fully carpeted basement, the **AlorAir Storm Elite** has more capacity. A small spill caught right away usually needs only a household 50-pint unit with a pump and a strong fan.
topPicksLead: The **AlorAir Storm LGR Extreme** is our top pick for drying wet carpet because it keeps removing water as humidity falls, pumps its own drainage and runs on an ordinary household outlet.

sections.heading: How to choose a dehumidifier for drying carpet

items.label: Know what kind of water it was
items.text: Clean water from a supply line is a drying job. Gray water from a washer or dishwasher means cleaning and a new pad. Sewage or outdoor floodwater means carpet and pad go, and a pro should handle it.

items.label: Size for the wet area, not the house
items.text: A small spill suits a household 50-pint unit. One soaked room suits a compact LGR around 80 pints AHAM. A carpeted basement needs an 85- to 125-pint LGR, or two machines on separate circuits.
sub: Close doors so the machine isn't drying the whole house
Our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) covers everyday sizing

items.label: Choose LGR for anything bigger than a spill
items.text: Low-grain refrigerant units keep pulling water as the air drops into the 40s, when ordinary units fade and the pad still holds moisture.

items.label: Get a pump
items.text: Carpet drying runs day and night for days. A pump to a sink, tub or window keeps it going while you sleep.

items.label: Budget amps for fans
items.text: A 15-amp circuit should carry about 12 amps continuously. A 5-amp LGR leaves room for fans; a bigger unit may need its own circuit. If you're living in the room, a lower-rated unit like the 6000Li is easier to put up with.

items.label: Measure, don't touch-test
items.text: Carpet can feel dry while the pad beneath is still wet. Use a pin moisture meter on the pad and subfloor and a [hygrometer](/best/best-hygrometer/) for the room.

blocks.caption: General guidance based on common restoration practice; your insurer or restorer may follow the IICRC S500 standard more specifically.

blocks.text: Carpet fibers dry fairly quickly; the foam pad does not. It holds water against the subfloor and is where odors and mold usually start. Pad is inexpensive, so when it's saturated, many pros cut it out and replace it once the subfloor is dry.

To dry underneath, restorers *float* the carpet: they pull an edge off the tack strip and blow air beneath it. Replace tack strip with rusty nails or crumbling wood, and keep drying until the subfloor reads the same as a dry area of the same floor.

A musty smell after a few days means something is still wet, usually the pad. Deodorizers only mask it. Find the wet spot with a meter and replace the pad if needed; our [musty smell guide](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-musty-smell/) and [mold guide](/guides/does-a-dehumidifier-help-with-mold/) cover what comes next.

sections.heading: How to dry wet carpet with a dehumidifier

items: **Stop the water and make the room safe.** Shut off the source and switch off the circuit at the panel if water reached outlets.
**Extract before you evaporate.** Make slow, overlapping passes with a wet/dry vac or rented extractor until you stop pulling much water.
**Move furniture and lift the edges.** Get furniture off the carpet, or set legs on foil or plastic blocks, then float the wet section off the tack strip.
**Set up airflow.** Aim fans, such as a Vornado 660 or rented air movers, low across the carpet and under any floated edge.
**Close the room and run the dehumidifier.** Shut windows and doors, set the unit to continuous and run the pump hose to a drain.
**Check twice a day.** Meter the pad and subfloor and watch room humidity fall. Most clean-water carpet jobs dry in about three to five days with proper equipment.
**Finish properly.** Replace pad or tack strip as needed, have the carpet re-stretched and cleaned, then set the dehumidifier to a normal 45–50%.

blocks.title: Renting vs. buying
blocks.text: For a one-time flood, renting an LGR and air movers can cost less than buying; if your basement floods every spring, owning pays off. See our [dehumidifier rental guide](/guides/dehumidifier-rental/), our [dehumidifier fan](/best/best-dehumidifier-fan/) picks and the broader [water damage guide](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-water-damage/).

items: **A wet basement carpet or two rooms after a pipe leak:** the AlorAir Storm LGR Extreme, with fans aimed low across the floor.
**One wet bedroom or living room upstairs:** the Dri-Eaz LGR 5000Li, light enough to carry and easy on the circuit.
**A flooded, fully carpeted finished basement:** the AlorAir Storm Elite, or call a restorer if it was floodwater.
**Drying a room you're still living in:** the Dri-Eaz LGR 6000Li for its lower rated noise.
**A small spill caught the same day:** the Frigidaire FFAP5033W1 plus a strong fan.
**Sewage, outdoor floodwater or wet walls:** skip the DIY and bring in a restoration company.

blocks.text: Saving wet carpet is a race against the 48-hour mark: extract first, float the carpet, move air across it and dry until the meter agrees. The **AlorAir Storm LGR Extreme** anchors that process in most homes. Go lighter with the **Dri-Eaz LGR 5000Li**, bigger with the **AlorAir Storm Elite**, quieter with the **Dri-Eaz LGR 6000Li**, and simpler with the **Frigidaire 50-Pint Pump** for small spills.

faqs.q: What is the best dehumidifier for wet carpet?
faqs.a: For most homes, the AlorAir Storm LGR Extreme: an LGR unit rated at 85 pints a day at AHAM conditions with a built-in pump. For a small spill, a household 50-pint unit with a pump is usually enough.

faqs.q: How long does it take to dry wet carpet with a dehumidifier?
faqs.a: A small spill can dry in a day or two. A soaked room or basement typically takes three to five days with extraction, air movers and an LGR. Stop when a meter shows the pad and subfloor are dry, not just the surface.

faqs.q: What size dehumidifier do I need for a flooded carpet?
faqs.a: For one wet room, an LGR rated around 80 pints a day at AHAM conditions. For a carpeted basement, an 85- to 125-pint LGR or two units on separate circuits. A household 50-pint unit only suits small, contained spills.

faqs.q: Do I need to pull up wet carpet pad?
faqs.a: If the pad is saturated or the water sat for more than a day or two, usually yes. Pad holds water against the subfloor and is where odors start, and it's inexpensive to replace. Gray water or sewage always means new pad.

faqs.q: Why does my carpet smell after it got wet?
faqs.a: Usually the pad or subfloor is still damp and bacteria or mold have started to grow. Meter it, replace wet pad, dry the subfloor fully and clean the carpet. Air fresheners won't fix it.

faqs.q: Is a carpet dryer the same as a dehumidifier?
faqs.a: No. A carpet dryer, or air mover, blows air across the surface to speed evaporation; a dehumidifier removes that moisture from the room. You need both for a wet carpet, or the evaporated water simply soaks into walls and furniture.
